# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10 (Bi-Vb Np10)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Np10
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10
**Title (English, from literature):** Exchanging designated personal property that was asked for
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Puggalikacetāpana* constitutes the tenth rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*. The rule stipulates that if a nun solicits a personal requisite for a designated purpose and subsequently exchanges it for something else, the requisite must be relinquished and the offense confessed. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Parallel formulations of the rule are widely attested across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bi-pm-np10) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (rule 10), as well as in the Bhikṣuṇī Vinayas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan. DharmaNexus registers substantial Pali-internal text reuse with related rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, sharing extensive passages with neighboring forfeiture rules such as *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 7, 9, 6, and 8, as well as several *Pācittiya* rules [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with Sanskrit Vinaya literature (including the *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and *Saṅghabhedavastu*) and Tibetan commentarial treatises, including the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112), and the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].
